changes.text:
+1 from a live implementer. We run an x402-gated API on Base (exact scheme) that started settling real payments this week, and these negative vectors are not theoretical for us:

**Settled-not-delivered — hit it in production testing.** The HTTP response to a paid call dropped after settlement had already completed on-chain. The payer saw a failed request; the payee's balance said otherwise. We only caught it by reconciling balances against our spend ledger. Any receipt format that assumes delivery implies settlement (or the reverse) will misclassify exactly this case.

changes.text: ATM's settled-not-delivered case is exactly the shape that two separate evidence planes are for. settlement-evidence-ref-v1 answers only whether the money moved — payer_debit/payee_credit recomputed from the rail's own receipt, never copied from the facilitator's SettleResponse — and says nothing about whether the action was delivered. Delivery is a separate claim, anchored separately (action_ref/AnchorRegistry). last_comment.author: Fizzl13
last_comment.text:
We implemented the single-payment part of this draft (§6, §7) in presign-guard, a pre-sign check for agent payments:

- POST /v1/check takes an optional mandate next to an EIP-3009 signature and turns a payment outside it red before the agent signs (wrong payer/asset/recipient, over perPayment or cap, expired, bad issuer signature, nonce ≠ binding).
- presign-guard-wallet's mandatePayer() makes x402 payments with the §7 binding as the EIP-3009 nonce.
- JCS bytes, digest, signature and the EIP-3009/Permit2 binding values match authority-vectors.json byte for byte.

Not covered: cumulative spend
